title: The Cellar Door
journal: Never-Writes-Twice says Fort Chalkmoth is a fort like any other, but a wounded Unbound scout told me to ask what moans in its cellar. This is my own errand, not that of my order, the Toh-Reel-Ka. The Toh-Reel-Ka's hunt for the Eye of Argonia (the old kings' jewel that can heal every sick Hist, at the Root, where the roots of every Hist meet under the sea) waits at Bell Station, whose divers know which drowned tower the marker stone shows, and either may come first. Fort Chalkmoth is the Archwardens' fort on the Chixathe Mesa above Noota Nara. I'm to get into the fort and see its cellar. The keep's door opens only with the wall captain's key and cannot be picked, so he may let me in, or I may find another way in unseen.
objectives: Get into Fort Chalkmoth's keep, by the wall captain's leave or unseen. (marker: Sakeeus-Wan, Door to Fort Chalkmoth Guardroom)

plan.going: The order hunts the Eye of Argonia, the old kings' jewel that can heal every sick Hist; it lies at the Root, where the roots of every Hist meet under the sea, and the Unbound want it first. This is my own errand, to see what moans in the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth; the order's hunt, at Bell Station, is open beside it and either may come first.
plan.next: Get into Fort Chalkmoth's keep, on the mesa above Noota Nara.
plan.ways: Ask the wall captain at the gate for leave, or go in unseen by the trapdoor in the yard.

answers: I am Toh-Wo, a Secret-Speaker of the Toh-Reel-Ka. A wounded Unbound scout told me to ask what moans in the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth. My order hunts the Eye of Argonia, which can heal sick Hist. This is my own errand.
Get into the keep of Fort Chalkmoth and see its cellar.
Get the wall captain (maybe Sakeeus-Wan) to let me in, or find another way in unseen. The keep door is locked and cannot be picked. There is also a guardroom door.
I do not know who Sakeeus-Wan is or who the wall captain is, and I do not know what moans in the cellar. I can find out by talking to people here.

title: The Cellar Door
journal: The wall captain, Sakeeus-Wan, says a Toh-Wo may sleep in the barracks, but the keep stays shut to strangers while three Sarpa raiders rob the chalk carts on the western approach. I'm to kill the three raiders; then he will open the keep and pay me. I can still go in unseen by the trapdoor in the yard instead.
objectives: Kill the three Sarpa raiders on Fort Chalkmoth's western approach. (marker: Sarpa Raider, Sarpa Raider, Sarpa Raider)
Tell the wall captain the raiders are dead. (marker: Sakeeus-Wan)

plan.going: The captain will open the keep once the raiders on the western approach are dead.
plan.next: Kill the three Sarpa raiders, then tell the captain.
plan.ways: Fight the raiders (any weapon or magic), or skip the captain and go in by the trapdoor unseen.

answers: I am Toh-Wo of the Toh-Reel-Ka, checking Fort Chalkmoth cellar on my own errand. Captain Sakeeus-Wan keeps the keep shut while three Sarpa raiders rob chalk carts on the western approach.
Kill the three raiders on the western approach, then tell the captain for entry and 100 gold.
Kill the raiders for the captain, or go in unseen by the trapdoor in the yard. Maybe I could also pickpocket the keep key from the captain.
I do not know what the order keeps in the cellar store, or what moans there. I can only find out by getting in.

title: The Cellar Door
journal: I came up through the trapdoor in the yard into the cellar's guardroom, unseen. If the garrison sees me in here, they will attack. The stair from the guardroom climbs to the quartermaster's store. I'm to see what I can of the cellar: the store above, the gaoler at the stair's foot and the inner door.
objectives: Look at the stack of sap jars by the stair in the quartermaster's store. (marker: Stack of Sap Jars (Jal-Veesa Knot))
Speak to the gaoler at the foot of the cellar stair. (marker: Tsleel-Vaku)
Try the cellar door. (marker: Door to Cellar Door)

plan.going: I am inside unseen, in the guardroom below the keep. Being seen means a fight with the garrison.
plan.next: Three things, in any order: look in the store at the top of the stair, speak to the gaoler, try the cellar door.
plan.ways: Stay unseen; persuade the gaoler or test him with Illusion for more (optional).

answers: That door led me unseen through the yard trapdoor into the cellar guardroom. If the garrison sees me they will attack. I am still on my own errand to learn what moans in the cellar.
Look at the sap jars in the quartermaster store, speak to the gaoler Tsleel-Vaku, and try the locked cellar door.
Talk to the gaoler, inspect the jars, try or pick the cellar door, or sneak.
I do not know who Tsleel-Vaku is, what the Jal-Veesa Knot is, or why sap jars are stored here. I can ask the gaoler and examine the jars.

title: The Cellar Door
journal: Jars of Hist sap tied with the knot of the tree-minder of Jal-Veesa, the town whose sick Hist I first saw, are stacked by the cellar stair, in a fort with no Hist of its own. The order's gaoler turned me away from the inner door, Toh-Wo or not, and said Never-Writes-Twice keeps its key. Behind the door, something moans. Who is down there, and why the order feeds them sap, I cannot learn here. I'm to go back to the order's hunt for the drowned tower that Bell Station's divers know.

plan.going: The cellar holds people who moan behind a locked door, fed on sap from Jal-Veesa; Never-Writes-Twice keeps the key; why is an open question.
plan.next: Go back to the hunt at Bell Station, east of Lilmoth.

answers: The quest is done. I got into the cellar guardroom unseen. The order stacks Hist sap jars tied with the knot of Jal-Veesa tree-minder in a fort with no Hist of its own, and something moans behind the locked inner door. The gaoler would not let me through, and says Never-Writes-Twice keeps the key.
Go back to the order hunt: travel to Bell Station, an islet east of Lilmoth reached by boat, and ask the divers which drowned tower is cut deeper on the marker stone.
I could go to Bell Station, or find a way to get the key from Never-Writes-Twice later to learn who is down there.
I do not know who or what moans in the cellar, why the order feeds them sap, or what the Eye and the Root truly are. I may learn by asking Never-Writes-Twice, or from the key.
